To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a systematic optimization of CE‐MS parameters (capillary coating, background buffer composition, sheath liquid composition, and nebulizing gas pressure) leads to a method with a high separation efficiency and a high reproducibility for the analysis of intact proteins by CE and that this method is applicable to various proteins showing diverse characteristics (pI, molecular mass, and hydrophobicity).

capillary electrophoreses (CEs) are a powerful separation technique for the analysis of intact proteins and that the combination of CEs and electrospray ionization (ESI)‐MS (CE‐ESI‐ MS) allows a fast, sensitive and selective screening of intact proteins in a single run.

a capillary coating is necessary to improve the CE‐ESI separation of intact proteins and that the capillary coating influences the EOF, the migration times and peak shapes, and the signal intensities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an optimized method for the analysis and characterization of intact small proteins by CE‐MS.
the development of a screening method for intact proteins by CE-MS.
the improvement and validation of a CE‐ESIMS method for the analysis, characterization, and screening of intact proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method can be used as a screening tool for the characterization of intact proteins.
the optimized method is a powerful tool for the analysis of intact proteins and their isoforms.
CE‐MS has become an indispensable technique in the analysis of intact proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CE‐ESI MS is an excellent technique for the characterization of proteins.
the presented method allows the screening of intact protein mixtures in a short time with high precision, and the results obtained can be transferred to a quantitative analysis.

the CE‐ESI method is a very useful tool for screening of intact proteins, but it is not a suitable technique for the characterization of proteins with a low pI value, a high molecular weight or a low hydrophobicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CE‐MS can be a useful tool for the characterization of small intact proteins in the context of a screening procedure.
a reliable and reproducible CE‐ESI MS method can be developed for the analysis of intact proteins.
the method is robust and reproducible and allows for the separation of intact proteins of different pI and molecular mass.
